label: Engaged early Buddhist dhyana and mindfulness frameworks in codifying classical Yoga
description: Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras systematized yogic meditative absorption (samadhi) and affliction analysis in close historical dialogue with Sramana and early Buddhist contemplative psychology.
dialecticalTension: Synthesizes dualist Samkhya metaphysics with contemplative techniques parallel to Buddhist jhana.
historicalContext: Classical India (c. 2nd century BCE – 4th century CE).

label: Inherited Upanishadic inquiry into witnessing self (purusha) and meditative interiority
description: Building on Upanishadic debates over the imperishable witness (atman/purusha), Patanjali formalized practical disciplines to disentangle pure awareness from mental fluctuations.
dialecticalTension: Translates speculative Upanishadic metaphysics into an eight-limbed psychological praxis.

label: Systematized the eight-limbed discipline of ethical, attentional, and meditative transformation
description: Patanjali codified Ashtanga Yoga into eight progressive limbs culminating in samadhi, offering a rigorous taxonomy of cognitive habits (samskaras) and attentional training.
dialecticalTension: Frames liberation as systematic de-conditioning of cognitive fluctuations (citta-vritti).

label: Shankara authored the Vivarana sub-commentary engaging Patanjali’s yogic psychology
description: Advaita Vedanta integrated Patanjali’s contemplative discipline as a preparatory purification of mind while critiquing Yoga’s ultimate metaphysical dualism between purusha and prakriti.
dialecticalTension: Adopts Yoga’s mental discipline while rejecting Samkhya-Yoga dualism in favor of non-dual Brahman.

label: Informed Jung’s psychology of individuation, active imagination, and chakra-symbolism seminars
description: Jung studied Patanjali’s Yoga Sutras extensively in his 1930s ETH Zurich lectures, treating yogic psychology as a systematic Western counterpoint for depth-psychological transformation.
dialecticalTension: Adapts eastern meditative interiority into analytical psychology while warning against uncritical Western imitation.
historicalContext: Jung’s Zurich lectures on Kundalini and Patanjali (1932–1939).
